summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple sclerosis and a long-standing suprapubic catheter, was admitted due to leakage around the catheter site and associated fatigue. He had no fever or pain, but urinalysis showed elevated white blood cells, prompting initial empiric antibiotics. Urology exchanged the obstructed catheter in the emergency department. Given his lack of infection symptoms and a urine culture consistent with contamination, antibiotics were discontinued. He was monitored for 24 hours off treatment, remained stable, and was discharged home after two days. The final assessment was mechanical obstruction of the suprapubic catheter with chronic bacterial colonization, not active infection.
